question: timeouts
answer:
**Configuration.** `httpx.Timeout` stores four values in seconds: `connect`, `read`, `write`, and `pool`. `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_CONFIG` sets all four to 5 seconds. `Client` and `AsyncClient` accept a `timeout=` default, individual requests can override it, and `None` disables the applicable timeout. [httpx/_config.py](<work>/httpx-rules-official-codex/httpx/_config.py:72) · [docs/advanced/timeouts.md](<work>/httpx-rules-official-codex/docs/advanced/timeouts.md:1)

**Propagation.** `BaseClient.build_request()` puts the effective settings in `request.extensions["timeout"]`. Both clients call `_set_timeout()` in `send()` to supply the client default if that extension is missing. An existing timeout extension takes precedence. [httpx/_client.py](<work>/httpx-rules-official-codex/httpx/_client.py:340) · [BaseClient._set_timeout](<work>/httpx-rules-official-codex/httpx/_client.py:584)

**Enforcement.** The default sync and async transports forward the extensions to `httpcore`, which enforces the limits during connection establishment, individual reads and writes, and waits to acquire a pooled connection. These are per-operation limits, so a request can take longer than 5 seconds overall. The transport maps `httpcore` timeout exceptions to HTTPX exceptions, including during response-body streaming. [Sync transport](<work>/httpx-rules-official-codex/httpx/_transports/default.py:230) · [Async transport](<work>/httpx-rules-official-codex/httpx/_transports/default.py:374) · [Exception mapping](<work>/httpx-rules-official-codex/httpx/_transports/default.py:74)
